title: Companies Are Lying About AI Layoffs - Here’s the Proof
summary: Argues AI layoffs are cover for H-1B insourcing, offshoring incentives and stock-price games, while AI does replace some language-heavy roles.

assertions.quote: They're using AI as a cover for the real extent of their greed

verdicts.note: Analyses (e.g. Oxford Economics, Challenger data) find AI is a small share of cited layoff reasons and some 'AI' cuts track cost cutting; but some cuts do reflect real automation.

assertions.quote: Salesforce received 1,137 H1B visas ... Almost the same amount of people that they just laid off

verdicts.note: Offshoring and global capability centers are real cost levers, but visa counts don't map onto layoffs one-to-one, and rate cycles and over-hiring explain much of the decline; the causal claim is weakly supported.

assertions.quote: Many of the jobs being lost rely heavily on the English language ... content moderation, basic copywriting, and customer service

verdicts.note: Support and content roles show the clearest measured AI substitution (e.g. Klarna, freelance-writing market studies), though some firms reversed course.
Stanford 'Canaries' (2025) found ~13% relative employment decline for 22-25-year-olds in AI-exposed jobs, but rates, over-hiring correction and other macro factors also matter.
